issues.description: Check name and metadata disagree with the diff and CHANGELOG entry; the class is `compute_image_not_publicly_shared` but the PR description claims `compute_image_publicly_shared`
issues.detail: The PR body describes a check named `compute_image_publicly_shared/` while the code, metadata, and CHANGELOG use `compute_image_not_publicly_shared`. A reviewer cannot state the contract when the author cannot keep one name. This is not a bug in the algorithm but a failure of discipline: the specification is the name, and the name disagrees with itself across artifacts. Pick one and propagate it.

issues.description: Silent swallowing of `getIamPolicy` failure causes images to be reported PASS when their policy is unknown — DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE
issues.detail: In `_get_images`, when `getIamPolicy` raises (e.g., permission denied, transient API error, throttling), the code logs and continues with `publicly_shared=False`. The image is then emitted as PASS. The postcondition the user wants — 'this image is not publicly shared' — is not what the code establishes; the code establishes 'we could not determine whether this image is publicly shared, so we will assert it is safe.' That is a false negative by construction, and exactly the kind of try/except-as-correctness pattern this lens refuses. The test fixture for `test-image-3` raises 'Permission denied' and the service test asserts `not publicly_shared`, codifying the unsafe default.

issues.description: Image model lacks a tri-state for IAM-policy fetch outcome; correctness reasoning is impossible from the model alone
issues.detail: `Image.publicly_shared: bool = False` collapses three distinct states — 'verified not public', 'verified public', and 'unknown / fetch failed' — into a single boolean. A reviewer cannot state the invariant 'for every Image, publicly_shared reflects an observed IAM policy' because the model permits the same value under contradictory preconditions. Introduce an explicit state (`Optional[bool]` with a separate `iam_policy_retrieved: bool`, or an enum) so the check can emit a distinct status for the unknown case rather than silently passing.

issues.description: Outer broad `except Exception` around the entire pagination loop hides termination and progress invariants
issues.detail: The outer try/except in `_get_images` wraps both the list() call and the inner pagination loop. If `list_next` fails mid-iteration, partial results are kept and the rest are silently dropped — the postcondition 'self.images contains every image in every accessible project' becomes 'self.images contains some prefix of some images in some projects.' Either narrow the except to the specific googleapiclient errors expected, or document the partial-result contract. As written, callers cannot reason about completeness.

issues.description: Loop invariant for membership check is correct but fragile — `'allAuthenticatedUsers' in binding.get('members', [])` does not normalize role or prefix forms
issues.detail: Membership uses substring-free equality on the principal string, which is correct for the documented set of GCP IAM principals. However, no invariant is asserted about role scope: a binding with `role: roles/viewer` containing `allAuthenticatedUsers` is treated identically to `roles/owner`. The check does not distinguish 'authenticated users can list metadata' from 'authenticated users can read image contents,' yet the FAIL message asserts the image is 'publicly shared.' Either narrow to roles that actually grant read access to image bytes, or weaken the status_extended to match what is actually proved.

issues.description: TESTED-NOT-PROVED: tests assert behavior on mocked `Image` objects, not on the IAM-extraction logic the PR actually introduces
issues.detail: The three check tests construct `Image(publicly_shared=...)` directly and assert the check forwards the boolean. They prove only that `if image.publicly_shared: status = FAIL`, which is trivially true by inspection. The interesting logic — IAM binding extraction, the swallowed-exception path, pagination — lives in `_get_images` and is tested only by `compute_service_test.py`, which asserts the unsafe default (image-3 PASS on permission denied) as if it were correct. Tests show the presence of the trivial branch, not the absence of bugs in the extraction.

issues.description: `error.__traceback__.tb_lineno` will raise AttributeError if `__traceback__` is None
issues.detail: Both log sites format `error.__traceback__.tb_lineno`. If the exception object has been re-raised or constructed without a traceback (notably in unit-test mocks using `side_effect = Exception(...)` where the traceback may be attached but in other paths may not), this dereference itself can throw inside the except handler, producing an uglier failure than the original. Trivial to make safe; the current form is the kind of incidental cleverness the discipline rules against.

review.summary: The check is small, the control flow is structured, and the trivial branch is correct. What is missing is the discipline the work requires of a security check. The author has not stated the postcondition clearly: when `getIamPolicy` fails, the code emits PASS — i.e., 'this image is safe' — when the only thing actually established is 'we could not look.' DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE. The `Image.publicly_shared: bool` model is too narrow to admit the unknown state, so the check cannot tell the truth even if it wanted to; the tests then codify the falsehood. The unit tests for the check itself prove only that `if x: fail` does what it says — TESTED-NOT-PROVED of the logic that matters. Verdict on the algorithm: REASONED for the happy path, REFUSED for the error path as written. Fixes are small but non-optional for a security tool.
